events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: A Helping Hand

options.text: [character] experience might indeed prove a valuable asset.
Do not mistake me for some figurehead.

events.text: It feels as though all of [rival] goes quiet at the news of [character] death. The very air feels heavy as you, [character], attend your somber coronation. These are large shoes to fill, a thought clearly on the mind of many at court. From the nobility of [rival] comes the polite but insistent suggestion that [character], a steady hand in the last years, provide guidance and assistance as your reign begins.

events.author: Dale Kent
events.name: Achievement

options.text: Achievement.

events.text: Achievement

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: An Empty Throne

options.text: Order the expedition back to [city] at once.
Pay the men well and send them away.
Sneak away in the dead of night.

events.text: The next village you come across bustles with activity and bubbles with rumors. They say that [character] has died, leaving the throne unoccupied and [rival] leaderless. Members of the expedition have no interest in returning home, but [rival] needs you.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Ashvamedha

options.text: Begin the ritual.
I will not risk my reputation.

events.text: Across the years, many of the Vedic [religion] sacrifices have fallen out of fashion and out of favor. Yet there is one that still holds sway in the hearts of many. The Ashvamedha sees a horse left to wander freely across the lands of [rival] for a full year, guarded by the new ruler’s troops. Any can oppose your rule by challenging the accompanying warriors. If it lives and remains free at the end of the year, then it is sacrificed as a symbol of your prestige. Will the horse be set free?

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Balance of Power

options.text: We will assume control... reluctantly.
They must clean up their own messes.

events.text: Both the [family] and the [family] have suffered labor uprisings in the last month, and they come to us seeking insight. While they do not wish to surrender all authority, they need the court's help to organize their affairs. What shall we do?

events.author: Leyla Johnson
events.name: Chance for Peace

options.text: Yes, let us make a temporary truce.
Yes, let us exchange gifts of friendship.
Why should we make peace with filth like you?

events.text: The [tribe] have sent one of their leaders to attend your coronation. After the ceremony, he approaches you cordially. "We made war against your last ruler," he says, "but we have no quarrel with you. Will you accept our offer of peace?" What is your reply?

events.author: Leyla Johnson
events.name: Coronation Festival

options.text: The [family]'s songs and poetry.
The [family]'s feasts of exotic dishes.
The [family]'s marksmanship contest.

events.text: All three noble families have requested to plan your coronation festivities. By tradition, the host will present you with a gift that represents the family's values, as a reminder of their goodwill. Which family's gift will you accept?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Crowned in Faith

options.text: Accept the ways of [religion].
[religion] will no longer be the state religion of [rival].
Declare that your own [religion] religion will be adopted by all of [rival].
Attempt to balance the two faiths.

events.text: As the new [title] of [rival], you are now the leader for all [rival]. This includes acting as a figurehead for the state religion of [religion], a problem considering your own [religion] beliefs. Will you set aside your faith for the unity of the nation, or set [rival] on a new path?

events.author: Zorbaz
events.name: Dowager Regent

options.text: No. [character] wanted me to rule, not you.
Please take the throne, father. I...

events.text: The nation grieves the death of [character]. During the funeral, [character] approaches you, the young heir [character]. "My son," [character] wraps you in a warm embrace; tears flow from his eyes. "We have many enemies. Please, my son, allow me to act as your regent and handle matters of state until you come of age." How shall you respond?

events.author: Leyla Johnson
events.name: Foreign Delegation

options.text: Accept granite to build stelae carved with laws.
Accept steel to equip an elite guard.
Accept ebony to study its strange properties.

outcomes.label: Succession Family Delegation Kill New
Succession Family Delegation Kill

events.text: Your coronation brings delegations from all across [rival]. These subjects have brought a selection of fine gifts from their home villages. However, the visitors stipulate that they will only give their gifts if they will be used in great royal works. What gift should we accept?

events.author: Zorbaz
events.name: Grandfather Regent

options.text: No. [character] wanted me to rule, not you.
Please take the throne, grandfather. I...

events.text: The nation grieves the death of [character]. During the funeral, [character] hobbles towards you, the young heir [character]. "Oh, my poor grandson. Hush now, it will be alright." [character] wraps you in a warm embrace; tears flow from his eyes. "Please, allow me to act as your regent and handle matters of state until you come of age." How shall you respond?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Heir To War

options.text: Vow to Jupiter that you will not rest until [rival] lies in ruins.
No, it is time for the wars to end.

events.text: [rival] has cemented itself as an enemy of Rome. As you inherit the ongoing war from your grandfather, his determination and drive to see Rome overcome this threat falls to you. Public sentiment against the foreign nation continues to deteriorate further, with one politician ending every speech with the words ‘Carthage must be destroyed’. Will you see an end to the war against [rival]?

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Heir to Heir

options.text: Reply to [character] warmly and seek his favor.
Politely refuse, asking that future messages come from [character].
Use the correspondence to gather military intelligence.
Openly discuss the latest scientific developments.

events.text: Soon after your coronation, you receive a message from [character], heir to the [rival] throne. He sends his congratulations and well wishes. As the next in the line of succession, he believes that the two of you should establish a close, personal friendship. Dealing with [character] directly undercuts the [rival] [title], [character], which could endanger relations.

events.author: Zorbaz
events.name: Lawful Regent

options.text: No. [character] wanted me to rule, not you.
Please take the throne, uncle. I...

events.text: The nation grieves the death of [character]. During the funeral, [character] approaches and bows to you, the young heir [character]. "My young lord," [character] lowers himself to a knee and looks you in the eyes. "With the death of [character], the nation is at risk. Allow me to act as your regent. I will handle matters of state until you come of age." What shall we do?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Ma'at

options.text: Seek balance and harmony in the kingdom.
Truth must always be upheld.
Seek the strength to carry out her justice.

events.text: When Ra spoke, Ma'at was born. Although she has no temple and no following, the goddess of harmony and truth is the model that every [rival] attempts to live by so they may enter the Field of Reeds. This divine balance is especially important in the [title] of [rival]. As is tradition, you present the gods with an image of Ma'at upon your coronation. Which of her values will shape your rule?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: New Beginnings

options.text: The day will be both my wedding and succession.
The families are right, I must wait and do what’s best for [rival].

events.text: As your coronation approaches the matter of marriage is raised. The families want you to make a political alliance with your marriage, but this could be the perfect chance to be united with [character]. Will you marry for love?

events.author: Leyla Johnson
events.name: New Leaf

options.text: Throw a great feast in their honor.
Erect a monument to their founder.
Send them a lavish bribe of gold.
They deserve no special treatment.

events.text: It has come to your attention that the [family] family was often displeased with your predecessor. As the new ruler, you have a unique opportunity to regain the [family] favor. How shall you win them over?

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: News of Succession

options.text: It is time to embrace my destiny.

events.text: An exhausted messenger arrives from [city] carrying a scroll sealed with the royal sigil. The [title] has died, leaving [rival] in your capable hands. You return home from your expeditions and take the throne, ready to lead your people into a prosperous future.

events.author: Jeri Roys
conditions: Not Any Descendant Of Leader Us
Not Aunt Uncle Of Leader Us
Not Paternal Niece Nephew Of Leader Us
Not Maternal Niece Nephew Of Leader Us
events.name: Nothing Is Ever Easy

options.text: In time, [rival] and the court will come round.
My reign shall be short indeed if dissent is not quashed at the first signs.
The [rival] should prove a convenient enemy to unite [rival].

events.text: [character], [title] of [rival], at last. Your coronation, at least, shows a unified nation. Rivals, disaffected nobility, and allies of [character] are everywhere, however. [character] in particular is making inroads in leveraging his father's legacy into a rallying cry of opposition.

[character] in particular is making inroads in leveraging his husband's legacy into a rallying cry of opposition.

events.author: Velociryx
events.name: Passing the Crown

options.text: I graciously accept this honor, both for myself and for my descendants.

events.text: With the death of [character], the legendary Pschent Double Crown passes into your care.

events.author: Leyla Johnson
events.name: Patriotic Fervor

options.text: Organize a labor corps to improve lands.

tip: As leader: +5% Unit Trait Modifier / Infantry
As general: +10% Unit Trait Modifier / Infantry

options.text: Train with the army to increase morale.
Encourage artisans to move to our capital.

events.text: Your coronation has been met with a wave of patriotic fervor, as subjects from across the nation seek to serve the new ruler. How shall we harness this enthusiasm?

events.author: Brodie Frehlich
events.name: Power Struggles

options.text: [character] must be removed, permanently.
We cannot upset [family] but will investigate carefully.
Instruct the [family] to get their own house in order before indulging in such rumour mongering.
We must tread carefully in these early days of rule. Let's meet with the two factions.

events.text: Your recent ascension to the throne of [rival] is overshadowed by family rivalries that formed during the reign of [character]. These matters dominate the discussions at court and the whispers of corridor intrigue and gossip. The most prominent issue has been raised by the [family] family. They claim that [character] has been siphoning state funds for [family] use.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Reclaiming Control

options.text: Welcome [city] back into the fold.
Permit their own rule.

events.text: The city of [city] has been living under its own guidance, away from the rule of [rival]. A council from the city visits soon after hearing of your coronation. They are favorable to your rule and offer to bring the city back under the sway of the crown. Will you accept this offer, or allow [city] to keep their Autonomous Rule?

events.author: Zorbaz
events.name: Regency

options.text: Of course, this is all for the good of the young king
My family are more than capable of handling my affairs were that to happen.

events.text: After seizing the regency of the young [character], you are taken aside by [character]. "I trust you will name [character] as your heir in the event of your untimely death." How shall we respond to this implicit threat?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Rightful Heir

options.text: The throne is mine!
It is time for [character] to return to the throne.

events.text: [character] is dead and you have been named [title]. However, things are not so clear cut. Your courtiers gasp and gesture meaningfully among themselves as [character] sweeps into the hall,. [character] looks you in the eye and speaks with a clear voice so that all may hear, "[character], you know that the throne is rightfully mine. Step aside so that I might take the crown that I was born to."

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Rightful Heir

options.text: This is what I was born for.

events.text: [character] is dead. With his stewardship ended, the crown has been returned so that you may become the [title] that you were always destined to be. May you serve [rival] well!

events.author: Leyla Johnson
events.name: Self-Reflection

options.text: I should focus on attaining righteousness.
I should surround myself with brilliant artists.
I should lead a quiet life of philosophical study.
I am already a perfect ruler.

events.text: The day of your coronation is at hand. Before the ceremony, you take some time to reflect on the responsibilities that come with the throne. It makes you question, what type of ruler do you aspire to be?

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Separation of Powers

options.text: That suits me just fine.
Offer [character] a very generous retirement.
Attempt to force him out.

events.text: The crown is yours, [character]. All the powers of that crown, however, are another matter. Through the end of [character] reign, [character] handled much of [rival] administration, and he shows no signs of wishing to relinquish those duties.

events.author: Leyla Johnson
events.name: Snake Signs

options.text: Sponsor chariot races in [city], the [family] seat.
Throw a banquet in [city], the [family] seat.
Host a contest of arms in [city], the [family] seat
No, I choose my own path.

events.text: The week before your coronation, a seer discovers a strange omen: one dead snake near the palace, with three living baby snakes in nests nearby. Startled, he interprets this to mean that you must hold the ceremony in one of the family seats. Which city do you choose?

events.author: Leyla Johnson
events.name: Taking the Crown

options.text: Host an enormous festival.

outcomes.label: Succession Taking The Crown Inquiry Superstitious
Succession Taking The Crown Inquiry Debauched

options.text: Conduct the traditional ceremony.

events.text: At last, the time for your coronation has come. Our advisors encourage you to keep the ceremony traditional, but you have mentioned several... unconventional ideas. Which would you like us to include?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: The Augurs

options.text: My rule will be blessed by the gods.
Celebrate with bread and games.

events.text: Before you take your throne, the three augurs, priests who divine the omens of the [rival] gods, seek to read the divine will of your rule. Reading the entrails of the birds, they finally they declare that your rule will see peace, good fortune, and well-being for [rival].

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: The Brink of Peace

options.text: A new era dawns.

events.text: It felt as though the Civil War would never end. Unending months of ambush and counterattack, starvation and cold, doubt and sacrifice. Yet here you stand, [character], King of [rival]. Not all who joined your insurrection will so quickly lay down arms, just because you now sit in [city], but most of [rival] is more than ready for a return to order and prosperity.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: The Brink of Peace

options.text: Peace is the priority. I will make what concessions I can to satisfy the other Rebels leaders.
Unity is the priority. [rival] cannot loosen its grip.

events.text: Students chatter in the hallways as you sit quietly upon your bed at the academy, wiping away tears. With the death of [character], fate thrusts you upon the throne. You no longer have time for your studies, as the business of ruling [rival] consumes every spare hour and the coronation arrives within the week. Steeling yourself to bear the burden of leadership, you decide you must...

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: The Dedication

options.text: I am Ahura Mazda's. Ahura Mazda is mine.
These are not my ways.

events.text: [character] approaches you soon after the rites for [character] have been observed. "The loss of [character] is a great blow for [religion] everywhere. Every person must make a choice of whether or not they will aid Ahura Mazda. I hope you make the right decision, as he did." Ahura Mazda offers aid but demands it in return. As the new ruler, do you continue the traditions of [religion]?

events.text: It is time for [character] to be laid to rest, but there are disagreements over how the leader wanted to be buried. Unlike most rulers, it seems like he made few preparations for eternity. As the new [title], it falls to you to decide [character] journey to the afterlife. How will you honor the fallen ruler?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: The Road to Glory

options.text: I will reshape this world to a new future.
No, it's too much pressure!

events.text: The annals of your dynasty's history is filled with great rulers, from [character] to [character]. But times are late and the world is changing. [rival] will need a ruler who can stand above all others to lead its people into the future. Will you, [character], aspire to stand atop the shoulders of those who came before you?

events.text: [character], [title] of [rival], at last. As you address the crowds in [city], on what shall you speak, to set yourself apart from [character]?
